financials_interim.notes: VONE COMPANY (standalone holding company) basis, three months ended 30 June 2026. The Company itself earns no operating revenue (pure holding-company model, income via dividends from subsidiaries) -- revenue, cost_of_sales, gross_profit, inventory left blank; 'Result from operating activities' Rs.2,048,510k is driven almost entirely by Dividend income of Rs.2,040,985k (+45.9% YoY from Rs.1,399,085k). EPS 1.82 = 2,077,843k/1,138,915,644 shares, exact. See GROUP row's notes for shared source/page citations and the discontinued-operations/cash-discrepancy findings, which do not affect the Company-only figures (Company has no discontinued operations and BS cash of Rs.659,202k ties exactly to the CF statement's closing cash of Rs.659,202k at Company level -- the BS/CF cash discrepancy noted for GROUP is a Group-level, LB Finance-driven item only).

Source: VONE Interim Financial Statements for the three months ended 30 June 2026 (filed CSE 13-Aug-2026). FYE 31 March (Note 1, p.8). Income statement/OCI p.3-4, balance sheet p.2, cash flow p.7, segment note (Note 12-14) p.11-12. GROUP (consolidated) basis. MAPPING: profit_before_tax=8,070,038 is the filing's own 'Profit before tax' line, which already sits AFTER a separate 'Tax on financial services' levy of Rs.1,582,681k (LB Finance's VAT/SSCL-type levy on financial services, netted between 'Profit before tax on financial services' 9,652,719 and 'Profit before tax' 8,070,038) -- consistent with the bank/finance-subsidiary convention used elsewhere in this DB (e.g. NTB). tax_expense=3,330,976 is 'Income tax expense' only. PBT-tax_expense=4,739,062 = profit from CONTINUING operations, not the stored profit_after_tax=4,732,141 (net profit for the period): the Rs.6,921k gap is a loss from DISCONTINUED operations (Valley View Ceramics LLC, wound up; Lanka Swisstek (Pvt) Ltd, held for sale -- both Lanka Walltiles/Lanka Tiles subsidiaries, Note 9) recognised net-of-tax below the income tax line -- a genuine, disclosed break in the simple PBT-tax=PAT identity, not an extraction error. EPS 2.42 (Group, attributable to parent) cross-checked: 2,757,241k / 1,138,915,644 shares = 2.42, exact. No current/non-current classification is presented on the Group balance sheet (typical for a group consolidating a licensed finance company, LB Finance) -- current_assets/current_liabilities left blank. short_term_borrowings=88,997,598 is 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' only; 'Due to banks' (121,452,040) and 'Due to customers' (195,592,298) are LB Finance's deposit/wholesale-funding lines, deliberately excluded as deposit-taking liabilities rather than corporate debt (same convention as NTB's 'Due to Depositors' exclusion) -- long_term_borrowings left blank as no maturity split is given. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: balance-sheet 'Cash and cash equivalent' (Group) = Rs.27,377,365k as at 30.06.2026, but the cash flow statement's own 'Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the period' = Rs.22,557,552k -- a Rs.4,819,813k gap, most likely because the BS cash line includes short-tenor placements/reverse repos at LB Finance that the CF statement excludes from its narrower definition of cash equivalents; both figures are taken directly from their respective statements as printed (not a column-swap -- verified against BS 'as at' columns and CF 'for the period' columns independently). cash_and_equivalents field stores the BALANCE-SHEET figure (27,377,365) per field definition (period-end position). capex=1,272,783 is 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment' only; a further Rs.21,679k was spent on intangible assets (not included in the capex field). SEGMENTAL: Finance segment (LB Finance) is a CONSOLIDATED SUBSIDIARY, not an equity-accounted associate -- 'Share of results of equity accounted investees' is immaterial (Rs.1,403k, from The Fortress Resorts PLC) despite the task brief's expectation of a large associate/bank-stake contribution; the Finance segment's PBT of Rs.6,152,814k (+40.1% YoY from 4,391,966k) drives the bulk of Group PBT growth as a fully consolidated line, not a below-the-line share-of-profit adjustment. All subtotals cross-checked against the segment note's Group column (Note 12, p.12) and tie to the primary statements.

thesis.thesis_text: Vallibel One PLC is a diversified holding company whose Group results are overwhelmingly driven by LB Finance, a fully consolidated licensed finance-company subsidiary (not an equity-accounted associate). Q1 FY2026/27 Group revenue grew 31.0% YoY to Rs.40,673.56mn (11% contract revenue growth plus 59% growth in LB Finance-driven interest income), Group PBT grew 44.0% to Rs.8,070.04mn, and Group PAT grew 50.0% to Rs.4,732.14mn, with LB Finance's segmental PBT of Rs.6,152.81mn (+40.1% YoY) the primary driver. The standalone holding company itself earns no operating revenue and is entirely dependent on Dividend Income from subsidiaries (+45.9% YoY to Rs.2,040.99mn). At Rs.90.50, P/B of ~0.56x and P/E of ~9.4x (annualised) are statistically cheap for this growth rate, and the dividend trend is improving (DPS Rs.1.00 to Rs.3.00 over FY2024-FY2026), but the concentration of Group earnings in a single subsidiary is the central risk to size against the valuation (interim FS, manual_a8b9e64ea7e5bedc, p.2-3, segment Note 12).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/credit-cycle data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). This is VONE's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this database for the current fiscal year (one quarter, no QoQ or multi-year trend available), so confidence is capped in the 35-55 range; a Rs.4,819.81mn balance-sheet-to-cash-flow cash discrepancy (likely LB Finance short-tenor placements) and the lack of current/non-current balance-sheet classification (typical for a group consolidating a licensed finance company) further limit precision here.

financial_quality.rationale: Group PAT grew 50.0% YoY to Rs.4,732.14mn on Group PBT +44.0% to Rs.8,070.04mn, with the Finance segment (LB Finance, a fully consolidated subsidiary, not an equity-accounted associate) contributing PBT of Rs.6,152.81mn (+40.1% YoY) -- the primary driver of Group profit growth. Group leverage (total liabilities Rs.445,187,993k vs total equity Rs.182,648,932k, debt/equity proxy ~2.44x) is elevated but largely reflects LB Finance's deposit/wholesale-funding base ('Due to banks' Rs.121,452.04mn, 'Due to customers' Rs.195,592.30mn), consistent with the deposit-taking-institution convention used elsewhere in this database (e.g. NTB) rather than corporate over-leverage.
citations: dividends VONE (FY2026 DPS 3.00, FY2025 DPS 3.00, FY2024 DPS 1.00)

growth_outlook.citations: Vallibel Group-affiliated diversified holding company whose Group profit is dominated by LB Finance, a fully consolidated licensed finance-company subsidiary contributing PBT of Rs.6,152.81mn this quarter -- as directed, this concentration is the central business-quality consideration: VONE's Group earnings quality and growth are effectively a leveraged play on LB Finance's lending-book performance, with the standalone holding company itself earning no operating revenue of its own (Company PAT driven 100% by Dividend Income, +45.9% YoY to Rs.2,040.99mn). Diversification exists (small stakes such as The Fortress Resorts PLC, and legacy ceramics subsidiaries now being wound down) but is immaterial next to LB Finance.

valuation.rationale: Group revenue grew 31.0% YoY to Rs.40,673.56mn, split between contract revenue (+11%) and LB Finance-driven interest income (+59% to Rs.20,475.02mn). EPS grew 41.5% to Rs.2.42, tracking profit-attributable-to-parent growth of +41.9%. Growth is real and broad-based (Group Result from Operating Activities +41% to Rs.10,336.75mn) but is overwhelmingly a single-subsidiary (LB Finance) story -- a Rs.6.92mn discontinued-operations loss from two small ceramics-related subsidiaries being wound down is a disclosed, immaterial below-the-line item, not a growth driver.

rationale: interim_updates VONE as of 2026-06-30 (yoy_json, segment note)
business_quality.citations: Discontinued operations (Valley View Ceramics LLC wound up; Lanka Swisstek (Pvt) Ltd held for sale) are transparently disclosed and quantified (Rs.6.92mn net loss), a governance positive. The Group's heavy dependence on a single subsidiary for the great majority of its earnings is itself a concentration risk that governance/board oversight at the holding-company level would need to actively manage, though this project has no disclosures/circulars feed to verify board composition or related-party terms between VONE and LB Finance directly.

governance_risk.rationale: At Rs.90.50, P/B is approximately 0.56x (Group total equity Rs.182,648,932k / 1,138,915,644 shares = Rs.160.40 BVPS) and P/E is approximately 9.4x on an annualised H1 EPS basis (Rs.2.42 x2 = ~Rs.4.84), both statistically cheap for a diversified holding company with a fast-growing financial subsidiary. Dividend history is improving: DPS rose from Rs.1.00 (FY2024) to Rs.3.00 (FY2025 and FY2026), a ~3.3% yield at the current price.

key_reasons: Group PAT grew 50.0% YoY to Rs.4,732.14mn on PBT +44.0%, with LB Finance (a fully consolidated subsidiary) contributing PBT of Rs.6,152.81mn (+40.1% YoY) -- the dominant driver of Group profit growth

Group revenue +31.0% YoY (Rs.40,673.56mn), split between +11% contract revenue and +59% LB Finance-driven interest income; EPS +41.5% to Rs.2.42; dividend trend improving (DPS Rs.1.00 to Rs.3.00 over FY2024-FY2026)
At Rs.90.50, P/B ~0.56x and P/E ~9.4x (annualised) are statistically cheap, but Group earnings quality is effectively a leveraged play on a single subsidiary, LB Finance, a genuine concentration risk
watch_factors: LB Finance's segmental PBT growth (+40.1% YoY) is the single most important variable in this thesis -- any slowdown in LB Finance's lending book or a credit-cycle setback there would flow through disproportionately to Group results

Group leverage (debt/equity proxy ~2.44x) is elevated, though this substantially reflects LB Finance's deposit/wholesale funding base rather than corporate debt -- worth distinguishing from operating-company leverage when assessing risk

The standalone Company earns no operating revenue of its own and is entirely dependent on Dividend Income from subsidiaries (+45.9% YoY) -- a structural feature of the holding-company model, not a one-off, but one that ties the parent's own cash generation to subsidiary dividend policy

horizon_notes.6m: Next interim will show whether LB Finance's PBT growth pace (+40.1% YoY) continues and whether the Rs.6.92mn discontinued-operations items (ceramics subsidiaries) are fully resolved.
horizon_notes.1y: If LB Finance sustains its current growth trajectory, the cheap P/B (~0.56x) and P/E (~9.4x) could re-rate; a slowdown in the finance subsidiary would be the most likely source of disappointment given its outsized share of Group profit.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on LB Finance's ability to grow its lending book through a Sri Lankan credit cycle without asset-quality deterioration, and on whether VONE diversifies its earnings base beyond this single dominant subsidiary.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/rate-cycle data source in this project to assess how a multi-year Sri Lankan interest-rate and credit cycle would affect LB Finance's net interest margin and, by extension, Group-level VONE earnings.

interim_updates.note_text: Vallibel One PLC (VONE) reported Group Revenue of Rs.40,673.56mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), +31.0% YoY (2025: Rs.31,056.16mn), split between Revenue from contracts with customers Rs.20,198.55mn (+11%) and Interest income Rs.20,475.02mn (+59%, driven by LB Finance, the Group's licensed finance-company subsidiary). Finance is a FULLY CONSOLIDATED subsidiary in this Group -- not an equity-accounted associate as might be expected of a diversified holding company's bank/financial exposure -- and its segmental PBT of Rs.6,152.81mn (+40.1% YoY from Rs.4,391.97mn) is the primary driver of Group PBT growth as a fully consolidated line; Share of results of equity accounted investees was immaterial at Rs.1.40mn (The Fortress Resorts PLC stake). Group Result from Operating Activities rose 41% YoY to Rs.10,336.75mn (2025: Rs.7,324.23mn). Group PBT (after a Rs.1,582.68mn 'Tax on financial services' levy specific to LB Finance, netted between 'Profit before tax on financial services' Rs.9,652.72mn and the reported 'Profit before tax' line) grew 44.0% YoY to Rs.8,070.04mn (2025: Rs.5,604.89mn). Income Tax Expense grew 42.0% YoY to Rs.3,330.98mn (2025: Rs.2,347.33mn), broadly proportionate to the larger pretax profit base. Net profit for the Period grew 50.0% YoY to Rs.4,732.14mn (2025: Rs.3,153.93mn) -- a Rs.6.92mn loss from DISCONTINUED operations (Valley View Ceramics LLC, wound up, and Lanka Swisstek (Pvt) Ltd, held for sale -- both Lanka Walltiles/Lanka Tiles subsidiaries) is recognised below the tax line and explains why PAT growth (+50.0%) outpaces the PBT-minus-tax identity for continuing operations alone (+45.0%). EPS grew to Rs.2.42 from Rs.1.71 (+41.5%), roughly tracking profit-attributable-to-parent growth of +41.9% (Rs.1,942.78mn to Rs.2,757.24mn) on an unchanged share count of 1,138,915,644. At the COMPANY (standalone holding-company) level, which earns no operating revenue and derives its result almost entirely from Dividend Income, Dividend Income grew 45.9% YoY to Rs.2,040.99mn (2025: Rs.1,399.09mn), driving Company PBT +46.6% YoY (Rs.1,430.07mn to Rs.2,096.36mn) and Company PAT +47.5% YoY (Rs.1,408.99mn to Rs.2,077.84mn); Company EPS Rs.1.82 (2025: Rs.1.24).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is VONE's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB for FY2026/27 (only a prior stale Sep-2025 document had been on file before this refresh; no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level items: (1) balance-sheet 'Cash and cash equivalent' (Group, Rs.27,377.37mn) does not tie to the cash-flow statement's closing cash figure (Rs.22,557.55mn), a Rs.4,819.81mn gap most likely reflecting LB Finance short-tenor placements/reverse repos included on the SOFP but excluded from the narrower CF definition -- both figures verified directly against their respective statements, not a column-swap; (2) no current/non-current split is presented on the Group balance sheet (typical for a group consolidating a licensed finance company), so current_assets/current_liabilities are left blank in financial_statements; (3) short_term_borrowings is 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' only -- 'Due to banks' (Rs.121,452.04mn) and 'Due to customers' (Rs.195,592.30mn) are LB Finance's deposit/wholesale-funding lines, deliberately excluded as deposit-taking liabilities rather than corporate debt.
interim_updates.takeaway: VONE's Q1 FY2026/27 growth (+31.0% revenue, +44.0% PBT, +50.0% PAT) is overwhelmingly a Finance-segment (LB Finance) story: LB Finance is fully consolidated, not an equity-accounted associate, and its PBT growth of Rs.1,760.85mn (+40.1% YoY) accounts for the bulk of the Group's Rs.2,465.15mn PBT increase. The standalone Company (holding-company) level tells a simpler, purely dividend-driven story: Dividend Income from subsidiaries grew 45.9% YoY, lifting Company PAT 47.5%. A small, disclosed Rs.6.92mn discontinued-operations loss (two ceramics-related subsidiaries winding down/held for sale) explains the gap between continuing-operations profit growth (+45.0%) and headline net-profit growth (+50.0%) -- not a red flag, just a genuine below-the-line item worth noting for anyone reconciling the PBT-tax=PAT identity.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.40,673.56mn, +31.0% YoY (2025: Rs.31,056.16mn): Revenue from contracts with customers +11% to Rs.20,198.55mn, Interest income +59% to Rs.20,475.02mn.

Finance segment (LB Finance, fully consolidated subsidiary) PBT +40.1% YoY to Rs.6,152.81mn (2025: Rs.4,391.97mn) -- the dominant driver of Group PBT growth; Share of equity-accounted investees immaterial at Rs.1.40mn.
Group PBT Rs.8,070.04mn, +44.0% YoY (2025: Rs.5,604.89mn), after a Rs.1,582.68mn 'Tax on financial services' levy on LB Finance; Group PAT Rs.4,732.14mn, +50.0% YoY (2025: Rs.3,153.93mn).

A Rs.6.92mn net loss from discontinued operations (Valley View Ceramics LLC wound up; Lanka Swisstek (Pvt) Ltd held for sale) is recognised below the tax line, a genuine disclosed item, not an extraction artifact.
Group EPS Rs.2.42 (2025: Rs.1.71), +41.5% YoY, on an unchanged 1,138,915,644 shares.
Company (standalone) Dividend Income +45.9% YoY to Rs.2,040.99mn, driving Company PAT +47.5% YoY to Rs.2,077.84mn (2025: Rs.1,408.99mn); Company EPS Rs.1.82 (2025: Rs.1.24).
key_drivers: LB Finance (Finance segment, fully consolidated) PBT growth of Rs.1,760.85mn YoY (+40.1%) is the single largest contributor to Group PBT growth of Rs.2,465.15mn (+44.0%).
Interest income growth of +59% YoY (Rs.12,853.27mn to Rs.20,475.02mn) outpaced contract-revenue growth of +11%, consistent with LB Finance's lending book expansion driving the Group top line.
A Rs.6.92mn discontinued-operations loss (two former ceramics-related subsidiaries) is a disclosed, quantified below-the-line item, not material to the overall PAT growth story.
